source_text: Delectat enim prorsus subantes animas infamare, quidquid umquam et usquam sanctorum fuit, ne clarorum operum castigentur exemplis.
pass_a_gloss: For it altogether delights lustful souls to slander whatever of holy people there has ever been and anywhere, lest they be chastened by the examples of distinguished works.

lemmas.lexica: LS exemplum; Blaise Adam as example not transmitter
LS anima; Blaise human soul as image

pass_b_english: For lustful souls positively delight in slandering every holy person who has ever lived anywhere, so that the examples of distinguished deeds will not rebuke them.

choices.why: Adam as example to later sinners, Julian's alternative to tradux.
Image of God in the soul; keep soul not 'mind' or 'life-force'.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
